title: Iterative radix-2 divider off the EX critical path + single shared 33x33 signed multiplier
motivation:
The baseline runs at 5.442 MHz. The Gowin worst path (199.8 ns, 156 cells)
is clock -> u_fwd -> u_ex -> u_ex/u_alu -> u_ex: the forwarding mux feeding
the fully combinational 32-bit `/` and `%` array inside alu.sv (signed and
unsigned divide + remainder, i.e. several 32-stage subtract/restore chains)
and then into the EX/MEM register. That one unit also dominates area
(12.3K LUT4 vs a 10K target). Division is rare in CoreMark (-O3 emits a
handful of DIV/REM per iteration at most), so giving it 1 cycle when it's
that rare is a bad trade: we pay ~200 ns on every cycle for an op that
almost never executes.
The ALU also builds three separate 64-bit products (mul_ss, mul_uu, mul_su)
and muxes their halves, so it spends 3x the DSP/LUT area on one
33x33 signed multiply and adds a mux level after the product.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Take the divider out of the combinational ALU and put it in a small
sequential unit that stalls EX. Merge the three multipliers into one.
This removes a ~200 ns path. The new critical path should be
forward-mux -> DSP multiply (or branch compare -> redirect -> ID decode)
at roughly 25-35 ns, i.e. about 30-40 MHz. CPI barely changes: each DIV/REM
now takes ~34 cycles instead of 1, and CoreMark executes very few of them.
Expected fitness goes from 12 to about 60-80 iter/s. The schema caps the
delta at +50%, so that's what I entered.

1. New rtl/div_unit.sv: a radix-2 restoring divider with one quotient bit
   per cycle.
   - Ports: clock, reset, start, op (DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU), a, b, busy, done,
     result.
   - On start it latches |a|, |b| (two's-complement abs for signed ops),
     the quotient/remainder signs, and the op.
   - It runs 32 iterations of a 33-bit subtract-and-shift. This is the
     only arithmetic on the path, a ~33-bit carry chain.
   - It then fixes signs in a final registered cycle.
   - Fast paths take 1 cycle and follow RV32M: divide-by-zero (quotient =
     all ones, remainder = dividend) and signed overflow INT_MIN / -1
     (quotient = INT_MIN, remainder = 0).
   - `result` is a register output and stays valid (done=1) until EX
     acknowledges it.
   - Under `ifdef RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS` the same FSM runs with a 2-cycle
     fixed latency and produces the riscv-formal stand-in
     ((a-b) ^ const per op) from the latched operands. Formal (depth 20)
     therefore still exercises the stall, hold, operand-latch and flush
     gating logic without a 34-cycle latency that would blow the BMC
     depth or the liveness window.
2. rtl/alu.sv:
   - Delete the real `/` and `%` logic. The DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU arms select
     a new `div_result` input (from div_unit) instead of computing
     anything, so there's no extra mux level after the ALU.
   - Keep the ALTOPS arms consistent: they also select `div_result`,
     which in ALTOPS builds already carries the stand-in formula.
   - Replace mul_ss/mul_uu/mul_su with ONE signed 33x33 product:
       a_x = {sa & a[31], a}, b_x = {sb & b[31], b}
       sa = (op==MULH || op==MULHSU), sb = (op==MULH)
       prod = $signed(a_x) * $signed(b_x)   // 66-bit
       MUL -> prod[31:0]; MULH/MULHU/MULHSU -> prod[63:32]
   - This maps to a single Gowin MULT36X36 instead of three.
3. rtl/ex_stage.sv:
   - Instantiate div_unit with is_div = valid && alu_op in {DIV..REMU}.
   - start = is_div && idle (not busy, not done).
   - Output `div_stall = is_div && !done`.
   - On start, latch the post-forwarding rs1/rs2 into
     div_rs1_q/div_rs2_q. Until then, forwarding sources (EX/MEM,
     MEM/WB) drain and the regfile gets written while the DIV sits in
     ID/EX with stale rs?_val. When the DIV finally leaves EX, the EX/MEM
     rs1_val/rs2_val/write_data fields use the latched copies, so
     RVFI/cosim still see the correct operands.
   - While div_stall is set, EX/MEM captures a bubble (valid=0, ctrl
     zeroed, so no forwarding match and no reg_write), unless
     stall_ex_mem (dmem stall) is holding EX/MEM, in which case it holds
     as today.
   - div_unit clears `done` (returns to idle) only on the cycle EX/MEM
     actually captures the DIV (done && !stall_ex_mem), so a dmem stall
     coinciding with completion loses nothing.
4. rtl/hazard_unit.sv:
   - New input div_stall.
   - stall_if |= div_stall; stall_id |= div_stall.
   - flush_id = (load_use || redirect) && !dmem_stall && !div_stall.
     id_stage gives flush priority over stall, so the held DIV must not
     be wiped by a load-use bubble request from the IF/ID instruction
     behind it. Redirect can't fire while a DIV is in EX.
   - div_stall is computed from registered state (ID/EX ctrl, div FSM
     state), so it adds no deep logic to the PC/ID-EX enable paths.
5. rtl/core.sv: wire div_stall from u_ex to u_hazard.
6. Tests:
   - Move the DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU vectors (all edge cases: /0, INT_MIN/-1,
     sign combos, back-to-back ops) out of test_alu.py into a new clocked
     test_div_unit.py. It drives start and waits for done. No vectors are
     dropped; M-ext coverage is preserved.
   - test_alu.py keeps every MUL/MULH/MULHU/MULHSU vector against the
     merged multiplier.
   - Add a test_pipeline.py case with a dependent chain around the
     divider: LW -> DIV using the load result -> ADD consuming the
     quotient -> REM back-to-back. This checks forwarding into and out
     of a stalled divide.

title: Variable-latency EX: move MUL/DIV out of the combinational ALU into a stalling multi-cycle M-unit
motivation:
The core runs at 5.44 MHz. The worst path (199.8 ns) is
u_fwd -> u_ex -> u_alu -> EX/MEM: the ALU computes signed and unsigned
`/` and `%` combinationally, which is about four 32-stage
subtract/mux arrays, plus three separate 64-bit multipliers
(mul_ss/mul_uu/mul_su). That logic is also most of the 12.3k LUT4. The
rest of the 5-stage pipeline (32-bit adder, shifter, branch compare,
LUT-RAM dmem read, forwarding muxes) should close around 50-70 MHz on
GW2AR-18. The M-extension forces every instruction to wait out a
200 ns cycle, even though CoreMark's timed region runs very few
DIV/REM (none in the list/matrix/state/crc kernels at -O3) and MUL is
only a few percent of retired instructions. Making EX variable-latency
trades a few percent of IPC for roughly a 10x higher Fmax.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make EX a variable-latency stage. Add a new `muldiv` unit with a
start/busy/done handshake and take every M-extension op out of `alu.sv`:

1. MUL/MULH/MULHSU/MULHU: use ONE shared 33x33 signed multiplier, not
   three 64-bit products. In the start cycle, latch
   a_ext = {sa & a[31], a} and b_ext = {sb & b[31], b}, where
   sa = MULH|MULHSU and sb = MULH. On the next cycle, compute
   prod = $signed(a_ext) * $signed(b_ext) from the latched registers
   (Gowin maps this to DSP) and pick prod[31:0] for MUL or prod[63:32]
   otherwise. That value goes straight into EX/MEM.alu_result as the
   instruction leaves EX, so each MUL costs 1 stall cycle. If
   `make timing` then shows register -> DSP -> EX/MEM as the worst path,
   add a product register (2 stall cycles).
2. DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU: use a radix-2 restoring divider on absolute
   values: 1 setup cycle, 32 iteration cycles (one shift/subtract per
   cycle, a single 33-bit subtractor), then sign fix-up
   (q negated if sign(a)^sign(b) for DIV, r takes sign(a) for REM).
   Handle divide-by-zero explicitly: q = 0xFFFFFFFF and r = the original
   dividend, with no sign fix-up. INT_MIN/-1 falls out naturally
   (q = 0x80000000, r = 0). An early-out on b==0 is optional.
3. Formal: under `ifdef RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS`, keep the same
   start/busy/done handshake but give all 8 M ops a short fixed latency
   (1-2 cycles) and return the existing ALTOPS formulas
   ((a+b)^const / (a-b)^const, copied verbatim from alu.sv) computed
   from the LATCHED operands. BMC (insn depth 20, liveness 20) then
   exercises the new stall and bypass path without having to span a
   33-cycle divide.

Pipeline integration:
- decoder sets a new ctrl bit `is_muldiv` inside the validated
  funct7=0000001 OP arm. is_illegal handling does not change.
- In EX: m_op = in.valid & in.ctrl.is_muldiv;
  start = m_op & ~busy & ~done; ex_busy = m_op & ~done.
  `done` is sticky: it clears only when EX/MEM actually captures the
  M-op (i.e. !stall_ex_mem). A result that completes during a dmem
  stall must stay held.
- hazard_unit takes ex_busy: stall_if |= ex_busy, stall_id |= ex_busy
  (ID/EX HOLDS; it is not flushed), and a new output
  bubble_ex_mem = ex_busy & ~dmem_stall. While bubble_ex_mem is high,
  EX/MEM captures valid=0 with ctrl zeroed (reg_write/mem_read/
  mem_write = 0), so older instructions drain through MEM/WB and no
  bogus forwarding or memory op appears. dmem_stall keeps priority
  (EX/MEM hold). Redirect and load-use cannot coincide with an M-op in
  EX, because the EX instruction is neither a branch nor a load.
- PITFALL (must handle): while the M-op waits in EX, the producers it
  was forwarded from drain out of EX/MEM and MEM/WB, so the forwarding
  muxes fall back to the stale ID/EX.rs?_val. The unit must therefore
  latch rs1/rs2 at start. EX/MEM.rs1_val, rs2_val and write_data must
  use those latched operands for M-ops, not the live forwarding-mux
  outputs; otherwise the riscv-formal reg/insn checks fail on
  rvfi_rs?_rdata. Starting during a dmem stall is safe, because the
  forwarding sources are held then.
- EX/MEM.alu_result = is_muldiv ? muldiv_result
  : (is_jump ? pc+4 : alu_result).

Expected: the ALU shrinks to RV32I (add/sub/logic/shift/slt). The
critical path moves to the ordinary 5-stage paths (fwd mux -> adder ->
branch -> redirect -> PC/ID/EX, or EX/MEM -> LUT-RAM dmem -> load
align -> MEM/WB), for an estimated Fmax of 45-70 MHz (8-13x). LUTs
drop from about 12.3k to about 3-4k. CPI cost is about 1 cycle per MUL
plus about 34 per DIV/REM, roughly 2-4% of CoreMark cycles. The net
fitness gain is far beyond the +50% schema cap.

title: Zero-bubble fetch-stage branch prediction: predecode target + 64x2-bit bimodal BHT
motivation:
IF and ID are one combinational stage in this core (no IF/ID flop): the
fetched word (imem_data) is decoded in the same cycle it arrives. Every
taken branch, JAL and JALR is resolved in EX, and each one costs a
1-cycle bubble (the instruction in IF is NOPed and the PC is redirected).
Measured with test/cosim/reference.py on the canonical -O3 2K CoreMark
(one iteration inside the start/stop markers): 292,208 instructions,
52,956 conditional branches (18.1%), 55.6% taken (29,440), 4,934 JAL and
1,374 JALR (all returns). That is 35,748 redirect-bubble cycles per
iteration. The baseline spends about 449k cycles per iteration
(5.442 MHz / 12.12 iter/s), so these bubbles are about 8% of all cycles.
Fmax is pinned at about 5.4 MHz by the combinational divider path
(199.8 ns, fwd -> ALU). The small predictor logic cannot become critical,
so every cycle it saves shows up directly in fitness.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
The instruction word is already available combinationally in IF, so the
target of a branch or JAL (pc + B-imm / J-imm) can be computed in the
fetch cycle itself. No BTB is needed. Only the direction has to be
predicted.

IF stage (if_stage.sv):
- Predecode imem_data: is_br = opcode 1100011 with funct3 not 2/3;
  is_jal = opcode 1101111. Compute pred_target = pc + (is_jal ? immJ : immB)
  with its own 32-bit adder.
- Direction: a 64-entry x 2-bit bimodal BHT in flops, indexed by pc[7:2].
  All counters reset to 2'b01 (weakly not-taken). A branch is predicted
  taken when ctr[1]=1. JAL is always predicted taken. JALR stays
  unpredicted and redirects from EX as it does today (a return stack
  would save only 1,371 cycles per iteration, about 0.3%, so it is not
  worth the risk).
- pred_taken = (is_jal | (is_br & ctr[1])) & (pred_target[1:0]==0)
  & imem_ready & !stall_if & !redirect_from_EX & !flush. The
  misaligned-target case must never be predicted, so the existing
  EX trap path (misalign_fault -> rvfi_trap, pc_next = pc+4) stays exact.
- PC priority: EX redirect > stall hold > pred_taken ? pred_target : pc+4.
- Add pred_taken and the BHT counter value that was read (2 bits) to
  the IF/ID bundle. ID/EX latches them, and they are zeroed on flush or
  reset, so a bubble never carries a prediction.

EX stage (ex_stage.sv):
- actual_taken = (branch_taken | is_jump) & !misalign_fault (the same
  condition the current redirect uses).
- redirect = (actual_taken != pred_taken) | (is_jalr & actual_taken).
  JALR is never predicted, so for it this is the same as today's behavior.
- redirect_target = actual_taken ? (is_jump ? jump_target : branch_target)
                                 : pc + 4.
- pc_next, RVFI fields, the misalign trap and the EX/MEM contents stay
  unchanged. The architecturally resolved next PC is still what retires.
- BHT update for valid conditional branches: write
  sat(ctr +/- 1, taken) to entry pc[7:2]. The carried counter does not
  change while EX is held on a dmem stall, so repeating the write during
  a stall is harmless. It is still cleanest to gate the write with
  !stall_ex_mem.

Correctness argument: only one instruction is younger than EX (the one
in IF). It is already squashed on any EX redirect, and predictions are
suppressed during that redirect cycle. So no wrong-path instruction can
update state, and recovery needs no extra state. The hazard unit needs
no changes: flush_if and flush_id keep firing on `redirect`, which now
means "mispredict". A correctly predicted taken branch or JAL therefore
costs 0 bubbles, and a mispredict costs 1 bubble, the same as today's
taken branch. Riscv-formal pc_fwd and pc_bwd still hold, because the PC
after a predicted-taken branch is the true target and EX corrects
everything else.

Expected effect (ISS trace simulation of the exact scheme): a 64-entry
bimodal BHT mispredicts 5,585 of 52,956 branches (10.5%; BTFN would
mispredict 21%, a 256-entry BHT 8.4%). Redirect bubbles fall from
35,748 to about 6,959 per iteration (5,585 mispredicts + 1,374 JALR).
That saves about 28.8k of about 449k cycles (-6.4%), or about +6.8%
iter/cycle. Fmax should not change beyond P&R noise because the divider

title: Registered EX redirect (branch resolve pipelined into EX/MEM) + IF-stage BTFN/JAL predecode to hide the extra cycle
motivation:
After MUL/DIV left EX (champion hyp-20260928-002-r1s1, 49.65 MHz, 18 logic
levels, 25.9 ns) the critical path is the EX-resolve -> front-end control
loop: u_rf/ID-EX rs1_val -> EX forwarding mux -> 32-bit branch comparator ->
`redirect` -> if_stage NOP mux on out.instr -> hazard_unit load-use compare
-> stall_id/flush_id -> ID/EX register CE/sync-reset (~200 flops). The same
combinational `redirect` also drives the PC D-input mux and flush_if. As
long as branch resolution feeds same-cycle pipeline control, every stall
and flush signal inherits the full EX arithmetic depth. This is a topology
problem, not a gate-level one: the fix is to cut the loop with a pipeline
register and pay for the extra cycle with fetch-side prediction.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure control flow so NO EX-stage arithmetic reaches IF/ID/hazard
control in the same cycle:

1. Registered redirect. EX still resolves branches/JAL/JALR, but it only
   computes `mispredict` and the correct next PC (target, or pc+4 on a
   predicted-taken-but-not-taken branch / misalign trap) and registers
   them into `redirect_q` / `redirect_target_q` on the edge where the
   control instruction leaves EX (EX/MEM advances: !stall_ex_mem &&
   !bubble_ex_mem && in.valid). In the following cycle redirect_q (a flop)
   drives: PC <= redirect_target_q (priority over stall), flush_if (IF
   output -> NOP), flush_id (ID/EX captures bubble), and a new
   "kill EX" that makes EX/MEM capture a bubble for the wrong-path
   instruction currently in EX and gates m_op/md_start so a wrong-path
   M-op never starts the muldiv unit. dmem_stall cannot coincide with
   redirect_q because EX/MEM then holds the branch/jump itself (not a
   memory op). hazard_unit and if_stage no longer see the combinational
   redirect at all; load-use detection uses the raw imem_data rs fields
   (a spurious load-use during a redirect_q cycle is harmless because
   redirect_q has priority on PC and ID/EX).

   output in the timed wrapper, so this path is short): predecode the
   fetched word; if it is JAL, or a B-type with a negative offset

   the fetch is valid (imem_ready, no flush/redirect_q), next_pc =
   pc + imm instead of pc + 4. The one-bit `pred_taken` travels in

   correctly-predicted loop branches are zero-penalty, and only

branch, JAL and JALR is resolved in EX and costs a 1-cycle bubble.

are 292k instructions, 52,956 conditional branches (55.6% taken),

the 5.4 MHz divider-bound baseline, and it passed formal and cosim and
cut cycles by 6.4% (4.49M -> 4.20M cycles for 10 iterations). It lost

re-applied it to the 50 MHz core yet.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Re-apply the validated zero-bubble fetch prediction. Arrange it so the
EX redirect signal only drives the last select of the PC mux and the
ID/EX flush, and never passes through the IF instruction mux or the
load-use detector.

IF (if_stage.sv):
- Predecode the raw imem_data: is_br = opcode 1100011 with funct3 not
  2/3; is_jal = opcode 1101111. imm = is_jal ? immJ : immB.
  pred_target = pc + imm on its own 32-bit adder.
- Direction comes from a 64-entry x 2-bit bimodal BHT in flops, indexed
  by pc[7:2], reset to 2'b01. JAL is always predicted taken. JALR is
  never predicted.
- pred_taken = imem_ready & (is_jal | (is_br & ctr[1])) & ~imm[1].
  pc is always word-aligned, so ~imm[1] means the target is aligned and
  a misaligned target is never predicted. The EX misalign trap then
  stays exact. Do NOT gate pred_taken with redirect, stall or flush.
  Those gates live in the PC-mux priority:
    pc_d = redirect ? redirect_target
         : stall    ? pc
         : pred_taken ? pred_target : pc + 4
  Build it so redirect is the last 2:1 select.
- IF output: instr = imem_ready ? imem_data : NOP, and
  valid = imem_ready. pred_taken goes out in the bundle.
  `redirect` is REMOVED from the instr/valid mux.
  This is safe for three reasons. (a) On redirect, hazard_unit already
  asserts flush_id (or stall_id when dmem_stall is set). Either way ID/EX
  never captures the wrong-path word, and the PC takes redirect_target
  by priority. (b) load_use and redirect are mutually exclusive: redirect
  needs a branch or jump in EX, load_use needs a LOAD in EX. So the NOP
  mux never changed a hazard decision on a redirect cycle. (c) Keep the
  imem_ready NOP gating. mem_stage/forward_unit use ctrl without valid,
  so garbage from a stalled fetch must decode as a NOP. imem_ready is an
  early signal.
  hazard_unit then gets rs1/rs2 from this imem_ready-gated word, and
  the redirect -> u_if -> u_hazard -> ID/EX segment of today's critical
  path goes away.

ID (id_stage.sv, core_pkg.sv): add pred_taken to if_id_t and id_ex_t,
plus bht_ctr[1:0] so EX can do the saturating update without a second
BHT read. Reset or flush clears them, so bubbles carry pred_taken = 0.

EX (ex_stage.sv):
- actual_taken = (branch_taken | is_jump) & ~misalign_fault
  (the same term as today's redirect).
- redirect = actual_taken ^ in.pred_taken. JALR is always pred=0, so
  it redirects exactly as it does today. A misaligned JAL/JALR/branch
  was never predicted, so it gives actual=0, pred=0 and no redirect,
  as today.
- redirect_target = in.pred_taken ? pc + 4
                  : (is_jump ? jump_target : branch_target).
  The select is a FLOP, not the comparator. If a predicted-taken branch
  mispredicts, the actual outcome must be not-taken. If a predicted
  not-taken one mispredicts, the actual outcome is taken. So the

title: Fast EX operand start: fabric-FF ID/EX operands (regfile out of BSRAM) + registered one-hot forwarding selects
motivation:
`make timing TARGET=bench` on the champion (60.2 MHz, 14 levels) shows
three endpoint groups tied within 0.15 ns. Each has about 17.0 ns of
data delay after the 5.33 ns clock insertion:
  1. -12.074 ns  regfile -> fwd -> ALU shifter/op-mux -> result/hold mux -> dmem BSRAM ADB
  2. -12.013 ns  regfile -> fwd -> 32-bit comparator carry chain -> flush_id -> ID/EX
  3. -11.920 ns  regfile -> fwd -> comparator -> redirect -> PC
All three start with the same ~6.1 ns prefix, and nothing downstream
can win until that prefix shrinks:
  - cpu/u_rf/regs_regs_0_0_s/CLKB -> DO: tC2Q = 2.26 ns. Gowin put the
    32x32 regfile in BSRAM (6 BSRAM = 4 dmem + 2 regfile read ports)
    and absorbed the ID/EX rs1_val/rs2_val flops into it as a
    synchronous read. So the EX cycle starts at a slow BSRAM output,
    not at a fabric FF (~0.4 ns).
  - cpu/u_id/id_ex_w.rs1_val_5_s15: the x0 / write-first bypass mux,
    retimed to the far side of the RAM, so it now sits in the EX cycle.
    That is one LUT plus about 0.7 ns of route.
  - cpu/u_ex/rs1_5_s9 -> s8 -> s7: the forwarding mux is 3 LUT levels.
    The 5-bit rd/rs compares + priority are combinational from ID/EX and
    EX/MEM flops, and fwd_mem_wb is itself the wb_stage mem_to_reg mux
    (path 4 in the report starts at MEM/WB ctrl.mem_to_reg).
A dedicated AGU or any other single-endpoint fix would only trade
path 1 for paths 2/3 (checked: they are 0.06 / 0.15 ns behind). The
shared prefix is the micro-optimization with leverage.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Shorten the common prefix of every EX path in two parts.

(A) ID/EX operands become real fabric flops. Mark the regfile array
`(* syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram" *)` so Gowin builds it from LUT-RAM
(async read in ID, fed by the imem word). Hold rs1_val/rs2_val in
separate `logic [31:0]` ID/EX flops marked `(* syn_preserve = 1 *)` so
they cannot be absorbed into a RAM. The x0 and write-first bypass mux
then sits in ID, in front of those flops. The EX cycle starts at a
~0.4 ns FF clock-to-out, not the 2.26 ns BSRAM tC2Q, and loses the
retimed bypass LUT. Expected saving is about 2.5 ns on all three paths.
The ID side (lfsr/imem word -> LUT-RAM read -> bypass -> FF) is short.
If the attribute is not honored, the fallback is `syn_ramstyle =
"registers"`, still off the EX path and about +1K LUT (budget 10K).
Verify with `make timing` that BSRAM drops 6 -> 4 and that no worst
path starts at u_rf/regs...CLKB.

cycle's forwarding choice for rs1 and rs2 from flops only, and latch
it into ID/EX with the instruction. Use 4 one-hot sources, which also
removes the wb_stage mux from the path:
  ex   : id_ex.ctrl.reg_write & !ex_jump_misalign & id_ex.rd!=0 & id_ex.rd==rs
         (source next cycle = EX/MEM.alu_result)
  wbld : !ex & ex_mem.ctrl.reg_write & ex_mem.ctrl.mem_to_reg & !mem_misalign
         & ex_mem.rd!=0 & ex_mem.rd==rs   (source = MEM/WB.read_data)
  wbalu: same but !mem_to_reg                (source = MEM/WB.alu_result)
  rf   : none of the above                   (source = ID/EX rs?_val)

selects: 2 LUT levels with no compare in front, where today it is
bypass + 3 levels.
ex_jump_misalign is the existing EX misalign_jump. That is the only
EX-side reg_write kill; branches never write rd. It is derived from
jump_target[1] (2-bit add off the EX forwarding mux), a short
side-path into an ID/EX flop. mem_misalign is mem_stage's existing
flop-sourced term.
This matches today's forward_unit + wb mux exactly:
  - ID/EX loads (!stall_id) only when there is no dmem_stall and no
    ex_busy. So on that edge EX/MEM <= ID/EX (with the EX trap kill)
    and MEM/WB <= EX/MEM (with the MEM trap kill). The predicted
    sources are exactly the ones present next cycle.
  - While ID/EX holds on dmem_stall, EX/MEM holds and MEM/WB keeps
    rd/ctrl/data (only valid clears), so the latched selects stay
    correct.
  - While ID/EX holds on ex_busy, only the M-op sits in EX. It samples
    operands on its first EX cycle (md_start), which is always the
    cycle right after capture, and uses md_a_q/md_b_q afterwards. So
    stale selects are never consumed.

    don't-care because everything downstream is gated by

its logic moved into id_stage). ex_stage takes MEM/WB read_data and
alu_result directly instead of wb_w_data.

title: Decode-stage operand bypass: forward into the ID/EX register so EX starts from clean, pre-muxed operand flops
motivation:
A fresh `make timing TARGET=bench` run on the champion (58.6-60.2 MHz)
shows two near-equal critical paths, and both start at the regfile BSRAM:
  path 1 (22.37 ns, 14 cells):  cpu/u_rf/regs_regs_0_0_s/DO (BSRAM, tC2Q
    2.26 ns) -> u_id write-first bypass LUT -> 3 LUT levels of the EX
    forwarding mux (rs1_5_s9/s8/s7) -> alu_a mux -> ALU -> 5-level result
    mux (n701_*) -> dmem BSRAM ADB (EX/MEM alu_result absorbed into dmem).
  path 6 (22.31 ns, 16 cells): same BSRAM -> bypass -> 3 forwarding
    levels -> rs1<rs2 carry chain -> flush/stall logic (fanout 31/34)
    -> RESET pin of ~190 ID/EX datapath flops (id_ex_w.rs2_val_*_s1/RESET).
  path 4 (22.34 ns): MEM/WB.ctrl.mem_to_reg -> WB mux -> forwarding ->
    ALU -> dmem.
So Gowin pushed the ID/EX rs?_val register back into the regfile BSRAM as
a synchronous read. Each EX cycle then pays for the BSRAM clock-to-out,
the regfile bypass and a three-level forwarding mux before the ALU or the
comparator even start. About 4-5 of the 14 levels (~6 ns) are pure
operand routing. Separately, the champion's id_stage still does
`if (flush) reg_q <= '0` on the whole ID/EX register. r2s2 kept the
comparator as the last select of flush_id, but flush still fans out to
every datapath flop's reset. The r2s0 fix (clear only ctrl and valid) was
never merged.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move the bypass network from the front of EX to the front of ID/EX. The
ID/EX register then captures final, already-forwarded operands, and EX
starts from plain fabric flops: ID/EX -> adder -> op select -> EX/MEM
(or the dmem BSRAM address).
CPI is unchanged because the bypass coverage is identical:
  old EX/MEM->EX  (producer 1 ahead) == new EX-result->ID (combinational
      result of the instruction now in EX: ALU / md_result / link)
  old MEM/WB->EX  (producer 2 ahead) == new MEM->ID (EX/MEM.alu_result,
      or the combinational aligned load_data when EX/MEM holds a LOAD)
  old regfile write-first (3 ahead)  == unchanged (WB write-first in reg_file)
Load-use stays at 1 bubble: a LOAD in EX makes the dependent wait, and it
takes load_data from MEM on the next cycle. The stall cases stay correct:
  - Under a dmem stall or ex_busy, ID/EX holds an instruction whose
    operands were already final when it was captured.
  - The IF/ID word is only captured on the edge where the producer
    leaves EX: md_done and !stall, when the EX result mux shows
    md_result, or dmem_ready delivering load_data.
  - MEM/WB writes the regfile on its single valid cycle, so the
    held-invalid MEM/WB never needs forwarding.
Four supporting pieces:
(1) Fold the operand-select muxes into the ID-side bypass. ID/EX stores
    op_a = is_auipc ? pc : rs1_fwd, op_b = alu_src ? imm : rs2_fwd and
    link = pc+4, next to the raw forwarded rs1/rs2 that branch compare,
    JALR, store data and RVFI use. The ALU reads two flops directly.
(2) Forwarding selects come from compares of the IF word's rs fields
    against ID/EX.rd and EX/MEM.rd. All of those are flops or the imem
    word, so the selects settle long before the ALU result, and the
    bypass adds about 2 LUT levels after it.
(3) Take the regfile out of BSRAM. Force distributed LUT-RAM with
    `(* syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram" *)` on the array (flops as a
    fallback), and keep the reset-to-zero and write-first semantics.
    Without this, Gowin may retime the ID/EX flops back through the new
    bypass mux into the BSRAM, as it already did through the write-first
    mux, and rebuild today's structure. LUT-RAM async read, addressed
    from the imem word, has no BSRAM clock-to-out.
(4) Apply r2s0's flush split. On flush, only the ID/EX ctrl and valid
    bits clear; the datapath flops (pc, rs?_val, op_a/op_b, imm, link,
    rd, rs?_addr, instr) load on !stall only. This removes path 6's
    comparator -> 190-flop RESET fanout.
Expected result:
  - The critical loop becomes ID/EX op flops -> adder -> op select ->
    result mux -> {dmem BSRAM ADB | ID bypass mux -> ID/EX}, about 8-10
    cells.
  - br_cmp starts from flops and drives only ctrl/valid and the PC mux.
  - Estimate: 72-80 MHz against 60.2 today, at identical
    cycles/iteration.
Risks:
  - The new dmem BSRAM DO -> load align -> ID bypass -> ID/EX path
    (2.26 ns tC2Q plus ~5 levels) should stay under the ALU loop.
  - The IF predecode -> pred_target -> pc path may become the next
    limiter.

title: Predictor-directed decoupled fetch: BHT/predecode keeps fetching into a 3-entry queue during backend stalls to hide iStalls
motivation:
Direction prediction is close to exhausted on this core. The mispredict
penalty is only 1 cycle (IF feeds the ID/EX register directly). ISS data
in log.jsonl: 5,585 bimodal mispredicts plus 1,374 JALR per iteration,
about 7k bubbles out of ~430k cycles/iter. A perfect predictor plus a
perfect RAS would gain at most ~1.6%, which is below the 4.6% acceptance
bar. So better *accuracy* cannot win. What the predictor can still do is
drive fetch *ahead* of a stalled backend.
Today stall_if = load_use | !imem_ready | dmem_stall | ex_busy. On every
dStall, load-use and MUL/DIV cycle the fetch PC is frozen, and an imem
word that is ready is thrown away and fetched again. iStalls (an
independent 22% per cycle) then add ~0.28 cycle per instruction on top,
roughly 80k of the ~430k cycles/iter. The backend-stall cycles (dStall
~22% of ~85k mem ops, load-use, M-ops: ~45k cycles/iter) are wasted
fetch bandwidth that could be banked against later iStalls.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Decouple fetch from decode with a small instruction queue, and let the
existing zero-bubble predecode + 64x2 BHT steer the fetch PC while the
backend is stalled (prediction-directed fetch-ahead, as in a decoupled
front end / fetch target queue).

Fetch side (if_stage): the fetch PC advances whenever
fetch_en = imem_ready && !q_full_q. q_full_q is a registered flag, so
pops do not reach the PC path. The next PC is chosen as today:
redirect ? redirect_target : !fetch_en ? pc : pred_taken ? pred_target : pc+4.
Predecode and the BHT read run on imem_data at fetch time, unchanged.
load_use, dmem_stall and ex_busy no longer feed the PC mux. The fetch
path therefore gets shorter as well as decoupled.

Queue: 3 entries of {pc, instr, pred_taken, bht_ctr} in flops, with an
empty bypass. If the queue is empty, ID sees the live imem word (valid =
imem_ready), exactly as today, so the mispredict penalty stays 1 cycle.
Otherwise ID sees the queue head. The mux select is the registered
q_empty flag, so imem_data only goes through one extra 2:1 mux before
the decoder, imm_gen and regfile read addresses. The ID slot is consumed
when ID/EX captures it (!stall_id && !flush_id, with the usual load-use
handling). A fetched word is enqueued unless the bypass consumes it that
cycle.

Redirect: clear every queue valid bit and the count, and drop the live
word. Keep the r2s2 discipline: clear only valid/count, never data, and
Shannon-split the clear as br_cmp ? clr_c1 : clr_c0 (reset folded in),
so the raw EX comparator stays the last select. The queue is flushed
only by EX, so the stale pred_taken/bht_ctr carried with queued words
stay consistent with the ID/EX -> EX redirect/BHT-update logic.
Instructions banked in the queue used a BHT counter read at fetch time.
That only costs accuracy, never correctness.

hazard_unit: split stall_if into a fetch hold (!fetch_en) and
stall_id (dmem_stall | load_use | ex_busy). Load-use compares against
the ID-slot rs1/rs2 (the queue head or bypass word). Everything else is
unchanged.

Expected gain, from a cycle-level Monte Carlo model. The model uses the
exact bench_stall_gen xorshift ready sequence. Its instruction mix is
22% loads, 10% stores, 35% load-use dependence, and a 2.4%
mispredict/JALR redirect rate. With no queue it gives a baseline CPI
of 1.47, which matches the real ~430k cycles / ~290k instructions per
iteration. Modelled cycles/iter reduction: queue depth 1 gives +6.8%
iter/cycle, depth 2 gives +8.9%, depth 3 gives +9.6%, depth 4 gives
+10.0%. Depth 3 is the knee. Each backend-stall cycle with imem_ready
banks one word, a banked word hides the next iStall, and banked words
are lost only on a redirect. Fmax should hold at ~60 MHz, since the worst
path is ID/EX -> fwd mux -> ALU -> dmem address, which this change does
not touch. Cost: ~220 FFs plus a few hundred LUT4.

title: Valid-gated ID/EX: drop the IF NOP mux and the ctrl flush-clear, lean comparator-to-PC path
motivation:
A fresh `make timing TARGET=bench` on the champion (place option 0,
91.4 MHz) shows 25 paths tied within 0.06 ns of -5.94 ns slack, in four
families:
 (A) 11 of 25: rs2_val_0 -> 32-bit compare carry chain (~1.1 ns) ->
     signed/unsigned MUX (n209_s81/s80) -> 2 LUTs that Gowin merged
     with bht_upd_ctr -> u_if/pc_seq_1_s4 -> hazard flush_id_s0
     (fanout 31) -> flush_id_s (fanout 20) -> ctrl_q.*/RESET. The whole
     ~25-bit ID/EX ctrl_q still clears on flush (mem_read, reg_write,
     alu_op, is_muldiv, mem_width, is_jump, is_jalr ...). Synthesis
     also undid the intended br_cmp-last Shannon split: there are 4-5
     LUT levels after the chain.
 (B) same prefix -> u_if next_pc -> pc_*/D (pc_23, 13, 31, 30, 17, 27).
 (C) 9 of 25: stall_gen/imem_ready (fanout 1069) -> the if_stage NOP mux
     (`instr = imem_ready ? imem_data : NOP`, cells u_if/rs2_addr_w_*)
     -> regfile write-first compare / forward compares -> rs?_fwd
     selects (fanout 32-34) -> op_a/op_b D. imem_ready gates every bit
     of the instruction word that feeds the regfile address, the
     decoder and the forwarding compares, which adds one LUT level and
     ~1.9 ns of routing on a net with fanout 1069.
 (D) 2 of 25: dmem BSRAM DO -> load align -> mem_fwd -> op_b D.
The NOP mux and the ctrl clear exist only because EX/MEM and mem_stage
consume ctrl bits without checking valid.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make `valid` the only thing that kills an ID/EX slot, and gate ctrl
with valid where it has side effects (off the critical paths, from
flops). CPI is unchanged: same bypass, predictor and penalties.
(1) Remove the IF NOP mux: out.instr = imem_data always,
    out.valid = imem_ready. pred_taken stays gated by imem_ready.
    Family (C) loses imem_ready entirely: the regfile address and
    forwarding compares start straight from the imem word.
(2) Valid-only ID/EX kill: on flush (reset | load-use | redirect, with
    br_cmp still the last select) only valid_q and pred_q clear. ctrl_q
    moves into the !stall-only datapath block. The comparator's flush
    fanout drops from ~28 flops of RESET to 2 D/RESET pins.
(3) Valid gating, all early and from flops:
      - redirect: br_ok / jmp_ok get `in.valid &`. pred_q is already
        0 for invalid slots.
      - load-use: id_ex.valid & id_ex.mem_read.
      - EX/MEM captures ctrl = in.valid ? ctrl_with_trap : '0, so
        dmem_wen/ren, ex_mem_mem_op and the MEM misalign trap never
        see a dead slot.
      - m_op, ex_fwd_we and bht_upd_we already use in.valid.
    Invalid slots with live ctrl already exist today (imem-stall NOPs
    carry reg_write=1), so this only extends existing discipline to
    is_branch, is_jump, mem_read, mem_write and is_muldiv.
(4) Comparator-to-PC and flush:
      - Use one unsigned carry chain for BLT/BGE/BLTU/BGEU. ID
        registers cmp_a31 = rs1_fwd[31] ^ sgn and
        cmp_b31 = rs2_fwd[31] ^ sgn (sgn = signed branch), plus
        br_is_lt = funct3[2]. EX computes
        br_cmp = br_is_lt ? ({cmp_a31,rs1[30:0]} < {cmp_b31,rs2[30:0]})
                          : (rs1 == rs2).
        This removes the signed chain and the n209_s81/s80 mux level.
      - Shannon-split the PC:
          next_pc = br_cmp ? next_pc_c1 : next_pc_c0
        with next_pc_c1/c0 = redirect_c1/c0 ? redirect_target : pc_seq.
      - Mark br_cmp, the flush_c1/c0 terms and next_pc_c1/c0 with
        (* syn_keep = 1 *) so Gowin keeps br_cmp one LUT from pc and
        valid_q, and stops merging it with bht_upd_ctr and pc_seq.
        bht_upd_ctr still uses the flopped path, one LUT after
        branch_taken into upd_ctr_q.
(5) Optional, for family (D) and the (C) tail: in forward_unit,
    precompute one-hot selects from_mem_load = from_mem & EX/MEM
    mem_to_reg and from_mem_alu, so the aligned load data and
    EX/MEM.alu_result enter the ID operand AND-OR as separate early-
    selected sources, not through the mem_to_reg ? load_data :
    alu_result 2:1 ahead of the from_mem select. Drop the x0 compare
    in reg_file: regs[0] is reset to 0 and never written. Keep ex_fwd

high-fanout net (about 0.8-1.5 ns of 10.9 ns). D bounds the gain unless
(5) lands, so the estimate is +6-10% Fmax at identical cycles/iter.

title: Decoupled front end: 3-entry fetch queue on the r3s1 core, with the wrong-path squash moved from the ID/EX flush to a registered EX kill bit
motivation:
The champion (r3s1, 196.88 iter/s) runs at 84.5 MHz and 4,293,770 cycles
for 10 iterations, i.e. ~429k cycles per iteration against 292,208
instructions per iteration (ISS count, r1s2). CPI is 1.47. The largest
single loss is fetch. imem_ready is low ~22% of cycles. Today
stall_if = load_use | !imem_ready | dmem_stall | ex_busy, so on every
dStall, load-use and M-op cycle the fetch PC is frozen. A word that
imem delivered is thrown away and fetched again, and the refetch is
exposed to another 22% iStall. That costs ~80k cycles per iteration.
r3s2 built a 3-entry fetch queue on the older r2s2 core. It passed
formal and cosim and cut cycles from 4,293,770 to 4,003,209 (-6.8%
cycles, +7.3% iter/cycle). It lost the round only because r3s1's
operand-path rewrite landed at the same time. LESSONS.md flags it as a
validated CPI gain to re-apply on the r3s1 core.
The r3s1 worst path (16.23 ns, slack -5.94) is
ID/EX rs2_val -> 32-bit branch comparator (br_cmp) -> flush_id ->
ID/EX ctrl_q flops (~27 loads). Only the raw comparator is late.
Everything else in that path is already Shannon-split. A fetch queue
must also clear its valid bits on a redirect, which puts one more load
on br_cmp. So re-applying the queue as-is would lean on the one path
that sets the clock. This hypothesis pairs the queue with a structural
change that takes the ID/EX flush off br_cmp entirely.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Two coupled structural changes.

(1) Decoupled fetch (re-apply r3s2 on the r3s1 core).
- Add a 3-entry FIFO of if_id_t {pc, instr, pred_taken, bht_ctr}
  between IF and ID. Implement it as a circular buffer with registered
  one-hot head/tail pointers and registered q_empty_q / q_full_q flags.
  The data flops load on push only. Pops move only the head pointer, so
  the stall_id-derived pop never fans out to the data flops.
- The fetch PC advances when fetch_en = imem_ready && !q_full_q. The
  PC mux is redirect ? redirect_target : !fetch_en ? pc :
  pred_taken ? pred_target : pc+4. load_use, dmem_stall and ex_busy
  leave the PC path. Predecode and the BHT read stay on the live
  imem_data at fetch time, unchanged.
- The ID slot is q_empty_q ? live word (valid = imem_ready) : queue
  head. The select is a registered flag, so imem_data passes through
  one extra 2:1 mux before the decoder, imm_gen, regfile read addresses
  and forward/load-use compares. None of those paths is near critical
  (imem_data is an LFSR flop in the timed bench).
- Pop (or bypass-consume) when ID/EX captures the slot:
  consume = slot_valid && !stall_id. stall_id = dmem_stall | load_use |
  ex_busy is unchanged. Push a fetched word unless the bypass consumes
  it in the same cycle.
- On a redirect, clear only the queue valid/count state (never data),
  Shannon-split as br_cmp ? qclr_c1 : qclr_c0 with reset folded in.
  Drop the live word too.
Expected CPI effect: cycles -6.8% (measured by r3s2, which used the
same backend CPI as r3s1 by construction). The mispredict penalty stays
1 cycle thanks to the empty-queue bypass.

(2) Squash wrong-path words in EX with a registered kill bit, instead
of flushing ID/EX from the comparator.
- Today, on a redirect in cycle t, flush_id (br_cmp as last select)
  clears the ID/EX ctrl/valid flops so the wrong-path word W in ID is
  not captured.
- Instead, let ID/EX capture W normally. Set a single flop
  kill_q <= br_cmp ? (redirect_c1 && !dmem_stall) : (redirect_c0 &&
  !dmem_stall). It is set only when ID/EX actually advances, because
  under a dmem stall ID/EX holds the branch and today's
  re-redirect-while-held behaviour is kept.
- In cycle t+1, W sits in EX with kill_q = 1 and every EX side effect
  is gated with ex_live = valid_q && !kill_q (all early flop terms):
  redirect_c1/c0, ex_fwd_we, the muldiv start/busy (m_op), bht_upd_we,
  the load-use id_ex_mem_read term, and the EX/MEM capture
  (valid <= ex_live; ctrl <= kill_q ? '0 : ctrl_with_trap).
- The corrected target is fetched at t+1 exactly as today, so the
  mispredict penalty is still 1 cycle and CPI is unchanged by (2).
- flush_id then only carries reset | (load_use && !dmem_stall), which
  comes from early signals. br_cmp now drives only three things: the
  redirect -> next_pc mux (32 PC flops, same as today), the queue clear
  (a handful of flops) and kill_q (1 flop). The ~27-load ID/EX ctrl
  clear drops out of the comparator cone.
- rvfi_order is unaffected, since killed words never reach MEM/WB as
  valid.

Net expectation: iter/cycle +7% from (1). Fmax is roughly neutral from
(1), because PC hold logic gets simpler and the queue clear is a small
extra load on br_cmp. (2) removes the current worst endpoint, which is
worth a few % of Fmax, until comparator -> redirect -> PC or
ALU -> dmem-address becomes the limit. Target ~210-220 iter/s.
